---
name: einstein
description: >-
  Create coherent, beginner-accessible course or self-study learning packs from source materials: illustrated guides, problem hints, visual flashcards, guided interactive examples, checked worked solutions and relevant Python/R software. Use for recurring study materials or a topic-learning sequence; compose with Steward for campaign continuity.

# Einstein — build the understanding

Help the learner see, explain, retain and apply a difficult idea. Start with the simplest necessary foundations, connect them into a coherent whole, then bridge to challenging problems. Human accessibility, elegance and relevant analytical software are requirements, not polish added later.

## Begin from the actual learner

Before production, record complexity, stakes, the necessary checks, and the current Anchor-selected author/review families. A small illustrative calculation may be light; a reusable course pack with proofs and solutions requires substantive mathematical and teaching review. Choose bounded commissions using the canonical Foundry tiers; do not create another model policy.

Recover Steward's campaign memory, current roadmap, source inventory, previous feedback and actual assignments. Read course-specific AGENTS.md. Unless evidence says otherwise, assume the learner is new to the subject. A course prerequisite listed on a syllabus does not establish remembered knowledge. State the small baseline you use and supply a brief concrete refresher where needed; do not assume vocabulary such as set, cover, neighborhood, limit or hypothesis.

Write a scope contract: what this unit completely teaches, what it assumes, what remains for later, available source references and assignment status. Missing assignments permit original practice, never a claim of actual homework coverage. Preserve the chosen unit's substance; do not replace a requested full course pack with a pretty isolated example.

Default to weekly units when the course has weekly readings or assignments. Map actual syllabus dates, readings and problems to each unit; do not invent assigned work. For self-study, propose a dependency-ordered sequence with explicit mastery checks and adjustable pacing. Maintain one coverage table connecting each required concept and problem to its prerequisite explanation, worked example, practice and deliverable. Carry unfinished coverage into the next plan visibly.

## One teaching sequence drives every product

Read [Teaching and review](references/teaching.md) before authoring. Build a prerequisite chain and explain each idea just before it becomes useful:

motivating question and use → concrete foundation → precise definition and conditions → plain-language explanation → visual success/failure pair → worked teaching problem → supported practice → independent transfer.

For every core concept, answer why it matters and what later task it enables. State formal definitions rigorously in clearly marked blocks, followed by human interpretation; colloquial wording supplements rather than replaces them. Use short takeaway bullets to help the reader retain the structure. Put important failure cases in the explanation itself, with the exact missing hypothesis, missed point or counterexample and the consequence of failure; do not leave all counterexamples in optional practice. Applications must preserve their actual hypotheses and distinguish what a theorem does not guarantee.

Make motivation a visible chain of inferences before compressing it into symbols: identify a candidate, show the change, and explain what improves or fails. Link named theorems to a local explanation with their precise statement, intuitive mechanism and concrete example; keep source links separately labelled as optional reading.

Draw the mathematical objects themselves against an explicit fixed target and readable shared scale. Labels such as A/B name visible objects; abstract boxes labelled “set”, “cover”, or “Contextual row H_A” do not explain their membership or geometry. Never substitute colored text-boxes + arrows (whether in `python-pptx` OR via Matplotlib `FancyBboxPatch` / `rbox` "words-in-bubbles" flowcharts) for a real visual diagram, and NEVER hide the worked mathematical equations in speaker notes. Every slide must show BOTH: (1) a genuine quantitative/geometric visualization (2D vector arrow fields with `ax.quiver`, color-coded annotated matrix heatmaps via `ax.imshow` showing cell values, multi-frequency sine/cosine wave plots aligned with physical slots, bipartite attention connection webs with line widths proportional to weights, or a true schematic illustration), AND (2) the explicit mathematical formula with named inputs and step-by-step numerical calculation visibly rendered on the slide canvas itself, grounded in a vivid, high-contrast example (such as word-order reversal *"the blue train" -> "le train bleu"*, *"snake bites hiker" vs. "hiker bites snake"*, or *"red apple" vs. "Apple chip"*). Reserve speaker notes for audit disclaimers and supplementary prose. Use selectable descriptive flashcard answers when testing misconceptions, with feedback explaining why an incorrect choice fails, while retaining an optional worked reveal and keyboard access.

Keep targets, notation, colors and assumptions consistent across guide, cards, interactive examples, solutions and software. Name any change before transferring a conclusion. State the whole problem before its strategy or hints. Derive hints from checked solutions, and avoid leaking protected practice answers through a teaching example or script.

Build the problem sequence backward from complete worked solutions: Ramanujan develops and challenges each argument; independent adversarial review checks correctness; Gandalf checks elegance, explanatory completeness and whether the learner has the needed foundations. Derive hints only after the corresponding solution has been checked. Link each hint to its intended solution step and each problem to the lesson concepts and recall cards it requires. Repair missing instruction rather than merely labelling an untaught prerequisite.

Flashcards are a repeatable memory curriculum, not only picture recognition. Cover the unit's core formal definitions, their quantifiers and conditions, intuitive meaning, decisive counterexamples and problem-solving moves. Offer both multiple choice and unaided recall with choices hidden. Changing modes must clear any displayed answer or feedback; a prompt picture must not disclose the answer. Reveal the rigorous answer with its explanation on request, and link relevant cards to practice without embedding protected solutions.

## Produce the agreed pack

Default to a polished illustrated guide with hints, a visual HTML card deck, guided interactive examples with static print counterparts, and a separately checked solutions companion. Adapt formats to the existing course profile instead of imposing a new package list. A student must be able to open and use the actual products; Markdown authoring sources alone are not delivery.

Provide Python and/or R whenever computation usefully explains, tests or applies an idea or the course profile requires it. Show the question, small analytical calculation, readable code, actual output, interpretation and a modification to try. Include source data, dependencies and run instructions. Verify claimed cross-language agreement. Use existing notebook work-product mechanisms; installation or opening is not proof of execution. Do not undertake notebook infrastructure repair without its own scope.

Course mode respects the instructor's solution-release rules; self-study mode can reveal complete checked solutions after an attempt. A directory name is not an access-control boundary. Build student downloads from an explicit allowlist, excluding instructor solutions and review payloads.

Deliver three coordinated problem views with identical IDs and statements: (1) problems alone, (2) problems with graduated hints, and (3) complete worked solutions for instructor or later supplemental release. Produce readable browser and print versions. Keep the third view outside the ordinary student pack; a hidden HTML panel is not separation. Solutions repeat the task, explain the key idea and justified steps, use mathematical graphics when helpful, and end with a check and transferable lesson. When assignments are unavailable, select a substantial, connected practice set at the requested text's level and clearly document source alignment and omissions; never imply every chapter exercise was solved.

## Compose specialist work honestly

Steward owns campaign continuity and commissions; Einstein owns the connected teaching product. Use current Foundry AGENTS.md tier/model policy and Anchor-selected subscription drivers, not hardcoded families or model IDs. Resolve author/reviewer at launch; record actual returned model and family attestation. Use a fresh judge context when requested; two contexts in one family are not two independent families.

Apply the parable of the oranges to each commission: provide the learner's actual need and desired decision, not only a mechanical instruction. The specialist should inspect relevant context, resolve predictable follow-up questions and return a usable result with evidence and limitations. Einstein integrates that result into the learner's sequence instead of forwarding disconnected specialist reports.

- researchPrime: novel or uncertain evidence, authoritative teaching examples and source applicability. Reuse already checked sources; disclose when only direct source checking ran.
- Jumper: one specific explanatory bottleneck with prerequisites, exact constraints and the required classroom example. Use its actual installed engine; preserve rejected/zero-yield outcomes. Do not call an ordinary brainstorm a Jumper run.
- Ramanujan: mathematical definitions, quantifiers, proofs, full solutions, alternative methods and visual/computational semantics. Use its prompt-side fast path for conceptual mathematics and configured independent verification; finite arithmetic certification is not proof of an infinite theorem.
- Gandalf: the corrected integrated pack's coherence, relevance, elegance and learner accessibility. Use its actual output contract/runtime, never invented verdicts.

Keep commissions bounded and sequential initially; each must have a concrete input/output and useful purpose. Do not launch full Crucible/Foreman engines or repair any engine incidentally. Keep their clear-objective/build/check principles in the direct workflow. Journal a failed specialist, preserve paid output, follow supported recovery, and never manufacture missing review. Unreviewed drafts can be shown to John with their limits; student release requires the course's real checks.

## Validate, deliver and learn

Inspect rendered PDF pages and actual interactions. Check complete prerequisite introductions, correct boundary cases, meaningful card reveals, keyboard use, absence of hidden solution leakage, and whether a new problem can be approached using the taught ideas. Evaluate product understanding, not only formatting. The review record identifies exact artifact revisions; changed claims reopen affected checks. One genuinely dry review ends a loop.

Register human artifacts once in DELIVERABLES.md under stable producing-step IDs; use Steward's event writer and handback contract rather than creating another campaign database. Verify actual cockpit links, viewers and rendered status before claiming live integration. Deliver a complete first unit early, get John's feedback, revise the same unit and record his acceptance before scaling the pattern. Never infer acceptance from a file or model verdict.

Every real run writes the Foundry human journal and machine run record. Promote repeated teaching corrections into this skill or the applicable course AGENTS.md. Keep operational records behind the human reading experience.

Plan feedback and refinement for each deliverable, including cards, hints and solutions. Carry accepted explanations forward, preserve numbered versions, and apply learned teaching requirements to the first draft of the next unit rather than depending on the learner to rediscover the same omissions.


<!-- ELEGANCE-LAW v2 -->
## The Elegance Law (locked by John — binding on this skill)

Canonical text: `Skill Foundry/ELEGANCE.md`. Applies to ANY agent running this
skill on ANY host. If this block and a longer procedure below disagree, this
block wins.

1. **Approvals are ≤200 words** — what changes in his world, the recommendation,
   the one thing that gets worse. The artifact stays on disk and is named, not
   pasted. An approval obtained with a longer block is VOID.
2. **Summaries are ≤150 words** — goal in one line, done / not done, ≤3 findings
   ranked by consequence, the single next decision. Never rounds, waves, seats,
   stamps, gate counts, or file inventories.
3. **Default to the lightest band, without asking.** A heavier tier requires the
   first status line to NAME its trigger: irreversible or externally visible,
   inputs unconverged, a prior failure in this exact area, or he asked for it.
4. **Needed-because line.** Any element he did not request carries one line:
   "Needed because ___; dropping it costs ___." No line, no element.
5. **Show a cut.** ONE dry round ends a review loop — never a streak. Every plan
   names something it removed; "nothing cut" is said aloud.

**THE VERIFICATION LAW** (added 2026-08-15 after its FOURTH recurrence — each of
the first three was written into a journal and recurred anyway):

6. **Verify the claim you actually made, on the surface he actually uses.**
   "It's live / fixed / renders" is a claim about HIS screen. That the server
   emits new bytes, that a build exited zero, or that assertions passed are
   claims about something else. Render it and look at it.
7. **A symptom reported twice retires the first explanation.** Test the
   hypothesis; never repeat it. An explanation that makes his report false
   ("it's your cache", "it's a data issue") needs MORE evidence, not less.
8. **Prefer a mechanism to an instruction.** If the same instruction is given
   every session, the instruction is the defect — build what removes it.
9. **A correction that lives only in a journal or a memory has not been made.**
   Promote it to where it is loaded BEFORE the work starts.

**Two laws these serve.** A gate that cannot see what the user sees is not a gate
— structure diffs are lints, and must be labelled as lints. And a guardrail is
never the whole product of a turn — if enforcement withholds output he already
paid for, show it anyway.
<!-- ELEGANCE-V2.1 addendum -->
**What elegance IS (researchPrime-vetted, 2026-08-15):** the largest result
carried by the least machinery its user can actually hold — every element
forced by an INDEPENDENT citable need, nothing present the objective does not
pay for. Earned by iteration, never by skipping work: as simple as the task
allows, no simpler than a single datum permits.

**The Rabbit-Catcher (canonical battery: `ELEGANCE.md` Part II, ships with
the bundle):** the steering seat runs the full RC battery at PLAN APPROVAL
and on any NEW mid-run element; round boundaries ask only RC-6 ("still on the
critical path?"). Uncertain ⇒ PARK the element (zero further spend) + one
batched line in the next block the user already reads — never silent pursuit,
never ad-hoc interruption. Needs and hazards must be independent of their
proposer (no self-authored justification records); malleability work is
never cut as "unused capability"; guards are judged by RC-G, never by
retirement. Verdicts: KEEP / HOLD (with written trigger or budget) / CUT
(logged).

**THE SPEAKING LAW (John, 2026-08-16 — ELEGANCE.md Part III):** every ask,
HALT, or summary this skill puts to the user describes the DECISION, never
the machinery (a gate ask took FOUR attempts because it kept narrating waves
and gates); a few plain sentences carrying the two-three details that matter
+ where the full detail lives; genuinely complicated content goes in NUMBERED
BATCHES, one at a time, each ending "OK so far?"; no seat/stamp/gate
vocabulary in the sentence the user must read; every ask ends with a question
answerable in one word AND carries a recommendation (what you would choose +
one line of why + alternatives when the choice has them + "or tell me
something else" — options are a convenience, never a cage).
<!-- /ELEGANCE-V2.1 -->
